title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #10

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which action shows attentive listening? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to a friend
   B. Looking at the speaker and staying quiet
   C. Looking out of the window
   D. Drawing on your desk

2. What is the difference between hearing and listening? (1 mark)
   A. They are exactly the same
   B. Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself
   C. Hearing is only for adults
   D. Hearing needs effort but listening does not

3. Which sentence has a plural noun? (1 mark)
   A. Mother buys sugar.
   B. Mother buys one mango.
   C. Mother buys three bananas.
   D. Mother buys a banana.

4. Where should you look to check an answer to a comprehension question? (1 mark)
   A. In another book only
   B. In your imagination only
   C. Back at the text
   D. At the ceiling

5. How can flashcards help with vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. They cost a lot
   B. They replace reading
   C. They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   D. They make words disappear

6. How should you sit when you write? (1 mark)
   A. With your back turned
   B. Straight, with your book in front of you
   C. Lying on the desk
   D. Standing on the chair

7. Which words show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. first, then, next
   B. sun, rain
   C. red, blue, green
   D. mother, father

8. Which is a mistake in reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Pausing at full stops
   B. Looking up at the audience
   C. Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   D. Practising first

9. Which word must begin with a capital letter in the middle of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. morning
   B. weather
   C. cloud
   D. Monday

10. What should you do to check the punctuation in your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   B. Tear it
   C. Write it again without looking
   D. Cover it

11. Which sentence needs a verb to be complete: Always ______ your hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. wash
   B. hands
   C. soap
   D. your

12. What do we do in a matching game with words? (1 mark)
   A. Draw a picture only
   B. Match each word with its meaning
   C. Sing a song
   D. Count the cards

13. What is the main idea of a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. The last word
   B. What the paragraph is mostly about
   C. The number of lines
   D. The title font

14. What can wall charts of similes and metaphors help with? (1 mark)
   A. Running
   B. Cooking
   C. Gallery walks and learning from each other
   D. Sleeping

15. What is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. A short wise saying that gives advice
   B. A type of number
   C. A page of a book
   D. A very long story

16. What does Asiyesikia la mkuu huvunjika guu teach? (1 mark)
   A. Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   B. Elders are always wrong
   C. Legs are weak
   D. Never walk

17. How can you find the meaning of a new word in a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Use the context and check a dictionary
   B. Tear the page
   C. Ask no one
   D. Ignore it always

18. What kind of word is when in When I arrived, the shop was closed? (1 mark)
   A. A conjunction
   B. A number
   C. A noun
   D. An adjective

19. The cow eats grass next to the river. Which word means the same as next to? (1 mark)
   A. beside
   B. inside
   C. under
   D. above

20. What is a group of lines in a poem called? (1 mark)
   A. A paragraph
   B. A stanza
   C. A chapter
   D. A sentence

21. Why should you mark pauses in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To hide words
   C. To spoil the page
   D. To know where to stop and breathe

22. Why are stories important in communities? (1 mark)
   A. They teach values and keep history
   B. They cause trouble
   C. They waste time
   D. They hide the truth

23. Which element tells where and when a story happens? (1 mark)
   A. Ending
   B. Character
   C. Setting
   D. Title

24. Which is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. Table
   B. Quickly
   C. Hurray!
   D. Beside

25. What is a hobby? (1 mark)
   A. A test
   B. A school rule
   C. Something you enjoy doing regularly in your free time
   D. A punishment

26. What is a good way to learn interjections in your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. Invent them
   B. Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   C. Ignore them
   D. Guess meanings

27. Which interjection shows surprise? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Ouch
   C. Wow
   D. Shh

28. Which is a mistake in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Forgetting the colon after the name
   B. Using a name
   C. Using a question
   D. Using a full stop

29. What should you do after writing a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Read it aloud with a partner
   B. Never look at it
   C. Tear it
   D. Hide it

30. Where can you find correct interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. By inventing them
   B. By copying from another language
   C. By guessing
   D. By listening to and asking elders and teachers

31. Which device is used mainly to take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Radio
   B. Clock
   C. Torch
   D. Camera

32. Which word in a small silver radio is the noun? (1 mark)
   A. small
   B. radio
   C. a
   D. silver

33. Which question should you ask about an advert? (1 mark)
   A. How many pages does it have?
   B. What is the paper colour?
   C. Who cut it?
   D. What is being sold and how much does it cost?

34. What does format mean for a form? (1 mark)
   A. Who wrote it
   B. How old it is
   C. What it costs
   D. How it is arranged on the page

35. What does N/A mean? (1 mark)
   A. Next assignment
   B. New address
   C. Not applicable
   D. No answer always

36. Why should you write true information on a form? (1 mark)
   A. False answers are best
   B. Forms are records and false information causes problems
   C. Nobody reads forms
   D. It is a game

37. Why is it important to obey leaders? (1 mark)
   A. It is a game
   B. It is boring
   C. It makes noise
   D. It keeps order, peace and safety

38. Why do leaders need to give clear instructions? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. So people know exactly what to do
   C. To make noise
   D. To confuse people

39. What does a red eight-sided road sign tell drivers? (1 mark)
   A. Park
   B. Go faster
   C. Stop
   D. Turn left

40. Which is a signal word for the second step? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. Finally
   C. Yesterday
   D. Next

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name two parts of an advert. (2 marks)

42. Write four numbered steps for crossing a road safely. (4 marks)

43. Explain when you would skim and when you would scan. Give one example of each. (5 marks)

44. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about why we should write neatly. Check your capital letters and full stops. (5 marks)

45. Write the plural of each English noun: plate, tomato. (2 marks)

46. Name two elements of a story. (2 marks)

47. Write a paragraph of four sentences about a time you handled money. Use when at least twice. (5 marks)

48. Describe how a class can start a reading club. (4 marks)

49. Give two examples of constructive leisure activities. (2 marks)

50. Write the verbs in this instruction: Close the door and sit down. (2 marks)

51. Explain what a stanza is. (2 marks)

52. Give two features of a poem. (2 marks)

53. Describe how a newsreader should read a weather bulletin. (4 marks)

54. Write one instruction from the road safety dialogue. (2 marks)

55. Divide into subject and predicate: My brother saves coins. (2 marks)

56. Give three rules for punctuating a dialogue. (3 marks)

57. Write two compound sentences about shopping using so and but. (4 marks)

58. Write two polite phrases to interrupt. (2 marks)

59. Explain what the proverb Many hands make light work means. (2 marks)

60. Rewrite correctly: we live in nairobi (2 marks)

61. Write two sentences using the interjections Hurray and Ouch. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Looking at the speaker and staying quiet
   Attentive listening means giving your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker.

2. B — Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself
   Hearing happens naturally, but listening is a choice to pay attention.

3. C — Mother buys three bananas.
   Bananas is plural, and the number three shows there are more than one.

4. C — Back at the text
   Good readers go back to the text.

5. C — They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   Flashcards are a simple tool for revision.

6. B — Straight, with your book in front of you
   Good posture helps neat writing.

7. A — first, then, next
   Sequence words show the order.

8. C — Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   Speed that is too fast loses meaning.

9. D — Monday
   Days of the week begin with capital letters.

10. A — Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   Reading aloud helps find where pauses and stops belong.

11. A — wash
   Wash is the action word that completes the sentence.

12. B — Match each word with its meaning
   The game links words to meanings.

13. B — What the paragraph is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

14. C — Gallery walks and learning from each other
   Charts display the sayings for review.

15. A — A short wise saying that gives advice
   Proverbs teach lessons in a few words.

16. A — Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   It means one who does not listen to the elders may come to harm.

17. A — Use the context and check a dictionary
   Context clues and a dictionary help.

18. A — A conjunction
   When joins two ideas by time.

19. A — beside
   Beside and next to both show the side.

20. B — A stanza
   A stanza is a group of lines.

21. D — To know where to stop and breathe
   Pauses help the listener follow.

22. A — They teach values and keep history
   Stories teach and entertain.

23. C — Setting
   Setting means place and time.

24. C — Hurray!
   Hurray shows joy.

25. C — Something you enjoy doing regularly in your free time
   A hobby is a regular enjoyable activity.

26. B — Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   Learning from speakers is reliable.

27. C — Wow
   Wow is used for surprise.

28. A — Forgetting the colon after the name
   The colon is needed after the name.

29. A — Read it aloud with a partner
   Reading aloud shows if it sounds natural.

30. D — By listening to and asking elders and teachers
   Speakers know the correct forms.

31. D — Camera
   A camera takes photos.

32. B — radio
   Radio names the thing.

33. D — What is being sold and how much does it cost?
   Buyers check product and price.

34. D — How it is arranged on the page
   Format is the layout.

35. C — Not applicable
   N/A means the question does not apply.

36. B — Forms are records and false information causes problems
   Honest answers are important.

37. D — It keeps order, peace and safety
   Obeying fair leaders keeps everyone safe.

38. B — So people know exactly what to do
   Clear instructions get work done safely.

39. C — Stop
   That shape is the stop sign.

40. D — Next
   Next shows the following step.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Headline, picture, description, price, contact details (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1. Stop at the edge. 2. Look right, left and right. 3. Listen for vehicles. 4. Cross when the road is clear.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in a sensible order.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Skim when you want the main idea, for example looking through an article. Scan when you want one fact, for example looking for a name on a list.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two situations and two marks for examples and one mark for correct meaning.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three neat, complete sentences, for example Neat writing helps others to read my work. It shows respect for the reader. I feel proud when my book is tidy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence, one mark for capital letters and one for full stops.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: plates, tomatoes
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two uses of when, for example When I reached the shop, I counted my money. When I paid, I received change. I was happy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear sentence and one mark for correct use of when.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect books, choose a name and a librarian, agree on rules for borrowing, meet regularly to read and share books, and record who borrowed each book.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reading, sports, drawing, singing, gardening, community service (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: close, sit
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem, separated from the next group by a space.
   Working / marking points: One mark for group of lines and one for separation.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Short lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, images (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Speak clearly, keep a steady pace, use a friendly and confident tone, pause at full stops and look at the audience.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look right, then left, then right again. (or Cross at a zebra crossing.)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a correct instruction and one for a complete sentence.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Subject: My brother. Predicate: saves coins.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name then colon, capital letter to begin the words, end with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark, a new line for each speaker.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: I had money, so I bought bread. I wanted a toy, but it was too costly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence and one for each correct comma.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Excuse me, may I say something? Sorry to interrupt, but could you repeat that?
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: When people share a task, the work becomes easier and faster.
   Working / marking points: One mark for sharing work and one for easier work.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: We live in Nairobi.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capital letters and one for the full stop.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hurray! We won the match. Ouch! I hurt my foot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.
